title: Flat complex descent from a fixed cartesian model
statement: Let $I$ be a small filtered category, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram of Noetherian rings, and $c$ a colimiting cocone with point $A$. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be of finite presentation [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Fix $i\in I$, a scheme $X_i$ of finite presentation over $\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$, and a cartesian square with top $g:X\to X_i$ and bottom $\operatorname{Spec}(c_i)$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $G$ be a bounded cochain complex of finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-modules, each flat over $A$ and with proper support over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Then there exist $j\in I$, $f_j:X_j\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_j)$ of finite presentation, a cartesian comparison $g_j:X\to X_j$, and a bounded complex $G_j$ of finitely presented modules flat over $R_j$ with proper support, together with isomorphisms $g_j^*G_j^n\cong G^n$ [def-pc-module-pullback] commuting with every differential. No perfect derived object is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Restrict to the filtered under-category of i and then a final directed poset, using Mathlib IsFiltered.exists_directed (Stacks 0032). Finality preserves the ring colimit. Choose one object of this nonempty poset and base change the fixed model to it. The cocone equations and pullback pasting identify X with the canonical pullback over that object.

Transport G to the canonical pullback using the inverse of the pullback isomorphism. The tensor-pullback adjunction makes the functor additive and preserves zero objects, hence boundedness. Cartesian tensor pullback preserves the finitely presented, flat, proper-support terms.

Apply finite_flat_proper_support_descent to the resulting directed system and transported complex. Return its stage through the final functor. Its model is a base change of the original fixed model; finite presentation is preserved. Pullback pasting gives its cartesian square with X.

The canonical baseChangeMap has the two projection equations. Pullback extensionality shows that its composite with the initial pullback isomorphism equals the new comparison from X. Tensor-pullback composition and identity give an isomorphism of pulled-back complexes with G. Take its components and use the cochain-map equation to obtain the required differential identities.

lean.statement:
theorem filtered_cartesian_flat_complex_descent
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ i : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj i)]
    (c : Cocone R) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec c.pt)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (i : I) (Xi : Scheme.{u}) (fi : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation fi] [QuasiCompact fi] [QuasiSeparated fi]
    (g : X ⟶ Xi) (hcart : IsPullback g f fi (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)))
    {G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ}
    (hGb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (G.X n))
    [∀ n : ℤ, (G.X n).IsFinitePresentation]
    (hGflat : ∀ n : ℤ, (G.X n).IsFlatOver f)
    (hGproper : ∀ n : ℤ, Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver f (G.X n)) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Xi : Scheme.{u}) (fi : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i)),
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation fi ∧ QuasiCompact fi ∧ QuasiSeparated fi ∧
      ∃ (hfi : LocallyOfFiniteType fi) (g : X ⟶ Xi),
        IsPullback g f fi (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) ∧
        ∃ (Gi : CochainComplex Xi.Modules ℤ),
          (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (Gi.X n)) ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ, (Gi.X n).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ, (Gi.X n).IsFlatOver fi) ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ, @Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver _ _ fi hfi (Gi.X n)) ∧
          ∃ e : ∀ n : ℤ, Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj g (Gi.X n) ≅ G.X n,
            ∀ n m : ℤ, Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackMap g (Gi.d n m) ≫ (e m).hom =
              (e n).hom ≫ G.d n m
